title: Chemical Equilibrium and Le Chatelier's Principle
description: A two-chapter introductory unit on chemical equilibrium adapted from version-pinned English Wikipedia articles. Chapter 1 builds the quantitative foundation — dynamic equilibrium, the equilibrium constant, the reaction quotient, the omission of pure solids and liquids, the link to the standard Gibbs energy change, and the temperature dependence of K. Chapter 2 develops Le Chatelier's principle as the qualitative response of a disturbed equilibrium: how concentration, temperature, volume/pressure, inert-gas, and catalyst changes shift (or fail to shift) the equilibrium position. This package is the controlled study corpus for a Coursewerk methodology evaluation; its demanding chemical notation (reaction arrows, equilibrium expressions, quantities) is chosen so fault-injection, cross-engine consistency, and revision-impact checks have checkable targets.
